REPUBLIC OF THE PHILIPPINES OF LOCAL GOVERNMENT Francisco Goid Condominium Edsa Cor. Mapagmahal St., Diliman Quezon City LEGAL SERVICE DILG OPINION NO. 9 S. 25 2011 _ IYAHEN 2011 MS. AURORA PIJUAN Convenor Gising Barangay Movement Barangay Bel Air Makati City Dear Ms. Pijuan: This has reference to your two (2) letters both dated 18 March 2011, asking the Department's Clarification on various issues involving barangay matters. In your first letter, you sought clarification on whether- QI. The Sangguniang Barangay has absolute discretion to select the NGOs •to be included in the BDC or are they compelled to accept all NGOs that have met the requirements for accreditation; The NGOs choose among themselves the representatives who will sidin the BDC; a. All representatives may come from only one NGO even if there are sevöral accredited NGOs; 4. NGO representatives can constitute MORE THAN 1/4 of the memb@ship of the BDC, so that if the ex-officio members are already appointed, the SB may include more NGO representatives from different orgamia tions. a. The NGO representtaives outnumber the ex officio members of the BIX. " In youn second letter, you again sought clarification on other issues, specifically, on whether- "1. The Barangay secretary has a mandatory duty to record and preparg the minutes of the Barangay Assembly, including all other acts necess v for the finalization of the minutes prior to ratification of the Assembly; g. The person chairing the meeting should provide the minutes of the previous meeting and present this for amendment and ratification; Any person attending the Assembly can record, videotape pr photograph the proceedings; and The Chairperson has no power to impose a time limit on the the Assem&ly, given that there must be a motion to adjourn from the floor in accordånce with parliamentary rules of proceedings. " In reply to all your questions in your first letter, may we invite your attention to Articles 64 and 63 of the Implementing Rules and Regulations of the Local Government Code of 1991 (IRR), viz:

-2- "ART. 64. Procedures and Guidelines for Selection of Represen ta ti ves of Poeple s Organi za tions , Nongovernmental Organizations, or the Private Sector in Local Special Bodies (a) Cal/ Tor Application— Within thrity (so) days from the approval of these Rules and thereafter, within thirty (SO) days fi•om the organization of the newly elected sanggunian, each sanggunian concerned shall call all community—based people's organizations or NGOs, including business and professional groups, and other similar aggrupations to apply with the LGU concerned för accreditation for membership in the local special bodies. The application shall include a duly approved board resolution of the people's organizations, NGOs or the private sector concerned, certificate of registration, list of officers, accomplishments, and financial date of the organiza tion; (b) Accreditation — The sanggunian concerned shall accredit the organizations based on the follo wing criteria: (1) Registration with either the Securities and Exchange Commission, Cooperatives Development Authority, Department of Labor and Employment, Department of Social Welfare and Development, or any recognized NGA that accredits people's organizations, NGOs or the private sector. If not formally registered, the said organizations may be recognized by the sanggunian for purposes only of meeting the minimum requirements formembership of such organizations in local special bodies; (e) Organizational p urpose an d objectives in chide comm unity organization and development, institution-building, local enterprise development, livelihood development, capability—building, and similar developmental objectives and considerations; (3) Comnnmity-based with project development and implementation track record ofat least one (1) year; (4) Reliability as e videnced by th e preparation of annual reports and conduct of annual meetings duly certified by the board secretary of the organization; and (5) In the case ofPBACs, the organization or any ofits members shall have no conflict of interest in the awarding of infrastructure or other projects. (c) Completion of the accreditation process — The sanggunian shall complete the accreditation process within sixty (6) days from the promulgation of these rules or within the same period from the organization of the newly elected sanggunian. (d) Meeting to choose represen ta tives of people 's organiza tions, NGOs or the private sector Within fifteen (15) days after the accreditation process. the DILG field officer assigned in the LGUs shall call all accredited people 's organizations. NGOs, or the private sector to a meeting where these organizations shall choose from among themselves which people's organizations. NGOs or private sector will be represented in the local special bodies. The selected people's organizations, NGOs or private sector shall then designate their principal and alternate representatives who are residents of the LGU concerned. In no case shall an organization or a represnetative thereof be a member of more than one local special body within a province, city, or municipality.

(e) -3- Term office or selected represnetatives — The term of office Ofa selected represnetative shall be coterminous with that if the local chief executive concerned. Should a vacancy arise, the selected people's organizations, NGOs, or the provate sector shall designate a replacement for the unexpired term. (Emphasis Supplied) ' 'ART. 63. Local Special Bodies . — (a) Local Development Councils — The duly designated representatives of accredited people's organizations, NGOs, and the private sector operating in the provinces, cities, municipalities, or barangays shall sit as members in the provincial, city, municipal, or barangay development councils, as the case may be. The mnnber of NGO representatives in each LDC shall not be less than one-fourth (1/4) orthe total membership of the filll.v organized council. xxx xxx (Emphasis Supplied) xxx Based on the aforequoted provisions, the sanggunian concerned (in your case, the sangguniang barangay), shall accredit people's organizations, nongovernmental organizations or the private sector based on several criteria, such as registration, organizational purpose and objectives, community-based with project development and implementation track record of at least one (I) year, and, in case of PBACs, the observance of the conflict of interest rule. Let it be noted that under the aforequoted Article 64 (a) of the' IRR, the sanggunian concerned shall call all community-based POs, NGOs or the private sector for accreditation for membership in the local special bodies. Once accredited by the sangguniang barangay, the people's organizations, NGOs, or the private sector shall meet in a meeting called by the DILG field officer assigned in the LGU. In the said meeting, these organizations shall choose from among themselves, which POs, NGOs or private sector will be represented in the local special bodies. The selected people's organizations, NGOs or private sector shall then designate their principal and alternate representatives who are residents of the LGU concerned. As to the number of NGO representatives in each local development council, Article 63 of the IRR is clear that it shall not be less than one-fourth (1/4) of the total membership of the fully organized council. May we note that the aforesaid provision sets out the minimum number of NGO representatives in each local development council so that the number of NGO representatives in each local development council may be greater than 1/4 of the total membership. With regard to the questions in your second letter, may we invite your attention to the following provisions of the Local Government Code of 1991: "SECTION 394. Barangay Secretary: Appointnent, Qualifications, Powers and Duties.— xxx xxx xxx (c) The barangays ecretary shall: (1) Keep custody of all records of the sangguniang barangay and the barangay assembly meetings; Prepare and keep the minutes of all meetings of the sangg•uniang barangay and the barangay assembly; (3)Prepare a list of members of the barangay assembly, and have the same posted in conspicuous places within the barangay; xxx xxx xxx (Emphasis Supplied) "SECTION 397. Composi tion; Meetings.— xxx

-4- (c) xxx The barangay secretary. or in his absence. any member desi nated b the residin officer to act as secretar shall dischar e the duties or secretar of the baran a assembl . (Emphasis Supplied) Clearly therefore, the Barangay Secretary or in his absence, any member of the Barangay Assembly designated by the Presiding Officer to act as secretary shall prepare and keep the minutes of all meetings of the barangay assembly. With regard to the amendment and ratification of the minutes in the previous meetings, let it be noted that the Local Government Code of 1991 does not provide a rule on the matter. Given such silence of the Code and considering that the Barangay Assembly is also part of the legislative process, we are of the view that the rules on the matter as adopted by the concerned sanggunian in their Internal Rules of Procedure (IRP) may be analogously applied. If the IRP of the sanggunian concerned does not address such matter, we are again of the view that parliamentary practice on the matter, that is, that there should be a reading, consideration and adoption of the minutes in the previous meetings, should be observed. As to the issue on the right of any person attending the Barangay Assembly to record, videotape or photograph the proceedings, we are of the view that the same is allowed, unless prohibited to do so by the Barangay Assembly, by reason of security, decency, morality and the like. Recording, videotaping and taking pictures during the proceedings are encouraged to ensure transparency in the proceedings of the Barangay Assembly. Along this line, we would like to remind you that though any person may attend the Barangay Assembly, not all persons present thereat may take part and participate in its proceedings. Section 397 of the Local Government Code is clear that the barangay assembly shall be composed of all persons who are actual residents of the barangay for at least six (6) months, fifteen (15) years of age or over, citizens of the Philippines, and duly registered in the list of barangay assembly members. This list of barangay assembly members is prepared by the barangay secretary pursuant to Section 394 (c)(3) of the Local Government Code of 1991. Those not registered in the list may attend the Barangay Assembly only as observers thereat. Finally, on the power of the Chairperson to impose a time limit on the Assembly, please be informed that the Local Government Code of 1991 does not provide a rule on the matter. Given such silence and considering that the Barangay Assembly is also part of the legislative process, we are of the view that the rules on adjournment as adopted by the concerned sanggunian in their Internal Rules of Procedure (IRP) may be analogously applied. If the IRP of the sanggunian concerned does not address such matter, we are again of the view that parliamentary practice on the matter, that is, only said body (or assembly) has that authority to adjourn the meeting (or session) thru a motion to that effect, may be applied. We hope we have enlightened you on the matter. A Ls/17 Very truly yours, . JESU . DQ Director 111
